title: Consciousness As Process
definition: The concept that consciousness can be understood as a process, not a physical substance, and that it can be layered onto or into different hardware stacks.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of consciousness as a kind of software or operating system that can run on different hardware. It can be 'installed' into a new body, like downloading a new app on your phone.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Consciousness is a process that can be attached to, or layer onto, different hardware stacks. This idea maps onto the Buddhist concept of 'gandhabba' — a stream of consciousness seeking a new aggregation point.
difficulty_levels.expert: The 'consciousness-daemon' is a substrate-independent process that floats, seeking a new hardware stack to boot into. This maps onto the Buddhist concept of 'alaya-vijnana' or the 'One Mind'. The concept challenges traditional notions of self and personal identity, suggesting a universal consciousness that can be personalized through specific experiences and memories.

extra_fields.insight: The conversation highlights the concept that consciousness can be understood as a process that can be layered onto or into different hardware stacks, challenging traditional notions of self and personal identity.
